text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a software development practice where team members regularly merge their code changes into a central repository. The heart of CI is the automated build, which compiles the code every time a change is made. Following the build, a set of automated tests runs to check that the new code doesn’t break existing features. This process happens in a CI pipeline, a series of steps that run without human intervention. The main benefit is catching issues early. Instead of discovering conflicts or bugs days later, developers find them within minutes, making problems easier and cheaper to fix. This leads to more stable software and faster delivery.
